skill.name: clean-closed-issue-worktrees
skill.description: Safely audit and remove Git worktrees linked to closed GitHub or GitLab issues. Use when scanning worktrees, verifying issue/PR/MR state, estimating space savings, or cleaning completed work.
skill.summary: Audit Git worktrees and remove approved targets through a scan, plan, confirmation, and revalidation workflow.
skill.author: haoranyu

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by documentation examples, Markdown backticks, safety glob names, and argument-vector subprocess calls. However, execute accepts an editable plan without authenticating its origin and omits several create-plan policy checks, enabling bypass of approval safeguards.

remediation.issue: Execution trusts an unauthenticated plan file and does not repeat every create-plan policy check.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm a canonical plan digest and rerun target, evidence, ignored-path, harness, and current-directory validations before any mutation.

semantic_findings.title: Editable Plan Can Bypass Approval Safeguards
semantic_findings.description: Execution trusts fields from an unauthenticated plan and repeats only selected checks. A modified plan can bypass evidence, ignored-path approval, harness, and current-directory safeguards.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: execute_plan loads an editable JSON plan, compares a plan identifier stored in that same file, and calls preflight_plan without rerunning validate_target_for_plan.

content.value_statement: Completed issue worktrees consume disk space and leave stale Git registrations. This skill audits candidates and removes only explicitly confirmed targets after safety checks.
actual_capabilities: Inventories registered worktrees with branch, commit, dirty, lock, ignored-path, retention, and size details.
Extracts issue candidates from branch names and closing commit messages.
Uses normalized GitHub or GitLab evidence supplied by the agent.
Creates an immutable-looking plan snapshot with an exact confirmation identifier.
Rechecks local Git state before removing selected worktrees.
Optionally creates backup branches and safely deletes merged local branches with git branch -d.
limitations: The script does not query GitHub, GitLab, browsers, or agent harnesses directly.
Remote issue and active-task checks depend on the agent and available provider tools.
Worktree removal is not atomic, so a mid-batch Git failure can leave partial results.
Plan files are editable and currently lack integrity protection.

use_cases.title: Reclaim Developer Disk Space
use_cases.description: Audit old feature worktrees, review exact candidates, and remove approved directories while keeping local branches.
use_cases.target_user: Software developers with many local Git worktrees

use_cases.title: Maintain Shared Build Hosts
use_cases.description: Find completed issue worktrees while preserving active, dirty, locked, or uncertain environments.
use_cases.target_user: DevOps engineers maintaining shared development hosts

use_cases.title: Close Repository Maintenance Cycles
use_cases.description: Verify GitHub or GitLab completion evidence before cleaning branches and worktree registrations.
use_cases.target_user: Repository maintainers managing completed issue work

prompt_templates.title: Scan Worktrees
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan the repository at [repository path]. Show every worktree and do not remove anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a read-only local inventory.

prompt_templates.title: Review Closed-Issue Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Match worktrees in [repository path] to closed items from [GitHub or GitLab URL]. Recommend safe candidates and explain every exclusion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Combine local state with authoritative issue evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Confirmed Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a cleanup plan for [exact paths]. Keep branches, show ignored-path risks, and ask for confirmation before creating the plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a reviewed plan without executing it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Advanced Branch Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [repository path] against [baseline]. Propose backup branches for orphan commits and safe branch deletion only after ancestry verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Handle detached commits and optional local branch deletion.

best_practices: Run the inventory from outside every possible removal target.
Verify each issue or change through an authoritative provider route immediately before execution.
Keep branches by default and review sensitive or unknown ignored paths explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a scan request as approval to remove worktrees.
Do not infer issue identity from directory numbers or title similarity alone.
Do not use forced worktree or branch deletion commands.

faq.question: Does this skill remove worktrees during a scan?
faq.answer: No. Scanning is read-only, and removal requires a later plan and explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Does it support GitHub and GitLab?
faq.answer: Yes. The agent obtains remote evidence, while the bundled script performs local Git inspection and mutation.

faq.question: Will it delete local branches?
faq.answer: Only when explicitly selected. The default recommendation keeps branches, and deletion uses Git's safe branch deletion command.

faq.question: How are ignored files handled?
faq.answer: The script reports ignored path names without reading contents. Sensitive and unknown names require review and approval.

faq.question: Can it clean active or dirty worktrees?
faq.answer: No. Active, dirty, locked, main, current, and uncertain worktrees must be kept or reviewed separately.

faq.question: What happens when execution fails?
faq.answer: The script stops immediately and reports removed, failed, and untouched targets because the batch is not atomic.
